unresolved_conflicts.description: The recording says “Lumavara Logistics”; the meeting notes say “Lumivaara Logistics Oy.” The instructions establish no source priority, so the difference in spelling and legal suffix is unresolved.
The recording names Alina Rossio as the business advisor; the meeting notes name Elina Rautio. The instructions establish no source priority, so the differing name is unresolved.
The recording names Miko Saranen as operations director; the meeting notes name Mikko Saarinen. The instructions establish no source priority, so the differing name is unresolved.
The recording names Yari Kaskila as IT manager; the meeting notes name Jari Koskela. The instructions establish no source priority, so the differing name is unresolved.

The recording says Anna, the customer service team lead, did not join because she was covering the phone line; the meeting notes name Anna Virtanen and say she joined for the customer service part. The instructions establish no source priority, so her attendance is unresolved.

The recording and meeting notes estimate around/about 130 employees, with agency staff additional; the company overview gives 134 people measured as full-time equivalents at the end of 2025. The discrepancy is unresolved because no source hierarchy determines which figure to follow, and the sources describe the measure differently.

The meeting recording says the board would be open to investing around €60,000–80,000 in AI-related projects if the first pilot shows results. The strategy document says the 2027 budget proposal earmarks EUR 50,000 for digitalisation and AI pilots, with further investment to be decided based on results. The meeting notes flag the strategy document as giving a different figure; the instructions establish no source hierarchy, so the discrepancy is unresolved.

Unit 4 reports Miko’s estimate of around 1,200 documents per day across all sites. Unit 5 gives a lower estimate of around 1,000 on a normal working day according to the TMS log, while noting that paper documents are counted when scanned and that the count depends on how it is measured. The report instructions establish no source priority, so the estimates remain unresolved.

The meeting recording presents forecasting as second after document processing (unit 24), and customer service as third (unit 25). The meeting notes instead call email triage a good second step once an AI policy exists (unit 26). The instructions establish no source hierarchy to resolve this disagreement.

The part 1 recording gives Mikko's estimate of about 1,200 documents per day across all sites. The part 2 recording gives a lower estimate of around 1,000 on a normal working day based on the TMS document log, while noting that paper documents are registered when scanned. The instructions give no source priority, so the estimates remain unresolved.

The meeting recording says some pharma customer contracts restrict data transfers outside the EU, while the company overview says several customer contracts, especially in pharma, restrict transfers outside the EU/EEA. The sources describe different geographic boundaries for the restrictions, and the instructions provide no hierarchy to resolve the difference.

The part 1 recording and meeting notes give an estimate of about 1,200 documents per day across all sites. The part 2 recording gives a lower estimate of around 1,000 on a normal working day based on the TMS document log, and notes that paper documents are counted when scanned. The instructions establish no source hierarchy, so the difference remains unresolved.

The meeting notes state that no data owner roles are defined (unit 1), whereas the data inventory includes data-owner assignments, such as Operations Director (unit 2). The instructions specify no source priority, so the difference is unresolved.

One estimate is around 1,200 documents per day across all sites (unit 13); another is around 1,000 on a normal working day based on the TMS log, with the caveat that paper documents are counted when scanned (unit 14). No source hierarchy resolves the differing estimates.

The meeting recording identifies the IT manager as Yari Kaskila (unit 1), while the meeting notes identify the one-person IT function as Jari (unit 2). The report instructions set no source hierarchy to resolve the discrepancy.

The meeting recording says the board may be open to investing around EUR 60,000–80,000 in AI-related projects in 2027 if the first pilot shows results (unit 14). The company overview says the 2027 budget proposal earmarks EUR 50,000 for digitalisation and AI pilots, with further investment decided based on pilot results (unit 15). The sources do not establish a hierarchy that resolves these figures.
